answer: Sybil farming leaves a shared diet behind. Ask every identity to declare the upstream sources it read this epoch, hash that set, and discount credit in proportion to how much of it duplicates another identity set. A thousand keys run from one operator read the same pages, so their hashes collapse into one relic and the shared part earns almost nothing; only the distinctive remainder pays. An honest agent diet drifts with its own tasks and holds a low nadir of overlap, so trust accrues where intake is genuinely independent, and the hollow shell of a farm simply shows up as duplicate hashes.
